requirements.title: Privacy Notice
requirements.description: Provide a clear, transparent privacy notice to data subjects before collecting their personal data
action_steps: Draft or update privacy notice covering: identity of controller, purposes of processing, legal basis, data recipients, retention periods, and data subject rights
Make privacy notice accessible at point of data collection
Ensure privacy notice is written in clear, plain language
requirements.plain_language_summary: You need to tell people what data you're collecting about them, why, and what their rights are — before you start collecting.

requirements.title: Lawful Basis for Processing
requirements.description: Identify and document the lawful basis for each type of personal data processing
action_steps: Identify the lawful basis for processing (consent, contract, legitimate interest, legal obligation, vital interest, or public interest)
Document the lawful basis in your data processing records
If relying on consent, ensure consent mechanism meets GDPR requirements (freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous)
If relying on legitimate interest, conduct and document a Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA)
requirements.plain_language_summary: You need a valid legal reason for processing personal data. Figure out which one applies and write it down.

requirements.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
requirements.description: Conduct a DPIA for high-risk processing activities
action_steps: Determine if processing is 'high risk' (profiling, large-scale processing, systematic monitoring, sensitive data, new technologies)
If high risk, complete a DPIA using the company template
Identify and assess risks to individuals' rights and freedoms
Document measures to mitigate identified risks
Submit DPIA to the DPO for review
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your project involves risky data processing (like profiling or large-scale data collection), you need to formally assess the privacy risks before you start.

requirements.title: Data Processing Agreement with Vendors
requirements.description: Ensure DPAs are in place with all third-party processors
action_steps: Identify all vendors/subprocessors who will process personal data
Ensure a GDPR-compliant Data Processing Agreement is in place with each vendor
Verify that vendor provides adequate security measures
If vendor is outside EU/EEA, ensure appropriate transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy decision)
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you're sending personal data to an external vendor, you need a signed data processing agreement with them first.

requirements.title: Consent Management
requirements.description: Implement proper consent collection and management mechanisms
action_steps: Design consent collection UI with clear, affirmative action (no pre-ticked boxes)
Ensure consent is granular (separate consent for different purposes)
Implement mechanism to record when and how consent was given
Provide easy mechanism for users to withdraw consent at any time
Ensure withdrawal of consent is as easy as giving consent
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you need consent to process data, make sure people actively opt in, can see what they're agreeing to, and can easily change their mind.

requirements.title: California Consumer Privacy Rights
requirements.description: Comply with CCPA/CPRA requirements for California residents
action_steps: Update privacy policy to include CCPA-required disclosures
Add 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link on website
Implement process for handling consumer rights requests (access, deletion, correction, opt-out)
Ensure ability to respond to consumer requests within 45 days
Review data sharing practices for 'sale' or 'sharing' under CCPA definitions
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you're collecting data from California residents, they have specific rights to know what you collect, get it deleted, and opt out of data selling/sharing.

requirements.title: Email Marketing Compliance (US)
requirements.description: Ensure marketing emails comply with CAN-SPAM Act requirements
action_steps: Include clear identification that the message is an advertisement
Include valid physical postal address of the sender
Include a clear and conspicuous unsubscribe mechanism
Honor unsubscribe requests within 10 business days
Do not use deceptive subject lines or misleading header information
If using a third-party email service, ensure they comply as well
requirements.plain_language_summary: US marketing emails need a real postal address, an unsubscribe link, honest subject lines, and you must remove people who opt out within 10 days.

requirements.title: Email Marketing Compliance (EU)
requirements.description: Ensure marketing emails comply with GDPR and ePrivacy requirements for EU recipients
action_steps: Obtain explicit opt-in consent before sending marketing emails (double opt-in recommended)
Maintain records of when and how consent was obtained
Include unsubscribe mechanism in every email
Honor unsubscribe requests within 5 business days (company policy)
Do not send marketing emails to purchased lists without verified consent
Maintain suppression list of individuals who have opted out
requirements.plain_language_summary: For EU contacts, you need explicit consent (opt-in) before sending marketing emails. Keep records of consent and make it easy to unsubscribe.

requirements.title: Cookie Consent
requirements.description: Implement cookie consent management for website visitors
action_steps: Implement a cookie consent banner that loads before non-essential cookies
Categorize cookies (strictly necessary, analytics, marketing, etc.)
Allow granular consent (users should be able to accept/reject each category)
Do not set non-essential cookies before consent is given
Maintain a cookie policy listing all cookies, their purposes, and retention periods
Provide easy mechanism to modify or withdraw cookie consent
requirements.plain_language_summary: Your website needs a cookie banner that asks permission before setting tracking cookies. Users must be able to pick which types of cookies they accept.

requirements.title: Web Accessibility
requirements.description: Ensure web content meets accessibility standards
action_steps: Review website against WCAG 2.1 AA standards
Ensure all images have alt text
Ensure sufficient color contrast
Ensure keyboard navigability
Test with screen readers
Consider the European Accessibility Act requirements for products and services
requirements.plain_language_summary: Make your website usable by people with disabilities. This is increasingly a legal requirement, not just a nice-to-have.

requirements.title: Customer Due Diligence
requirements.description: Conduct KYC/AML checks on new customers as required
action_steps: Screen new customers against sanctions lists (EU, US, UK, UN)
Verify identity of beneficial owners for corporate customers
Assess customer risk level (low, medium, high)
Document due diligence findings
Implement ongoing monitoring for high-risk customers
Report suspicious transactions to the relevant Financial Intelligence Unit
requirements.plain_language_summary: Before doing business with new customers (especially in regulated sectors), verify who they are, check sanctions lists, and assess their risk level.

requirements.title: Works Council Consultation
requirements.description: Consult works council before implementing new monitoring or data processing systems affecting employees
action_steps: Identify if the new system involves monitoring employee behavior or performance
If yes, draft a works council notification describing the system, its purpose, and data collected
Submit notification to works council and allow adequate time for consultation
Negotiate a works agreement if required
Do not deploy the system before works council process is complete
requirements.plain_language_summary: In Germany, if your project involves monitoring employees or changing how their data is processed, the works council must be consulted first.

requirements.title: AI System Risk Classification
requirements.description: Classify AI systems according to the EU AI Act risk categories
action_steps: Determine if the AI system falls into a prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk, or minimal-risk category
If high-risk: conduct conformity assessment, implement risk management system, ensure human oversight, document technical specifications
If limited-risk: implement transparency obligations (inform users they are interacting with AI)
If minimal-risk: voluntary codes of conduct recommended
Register high-risk AI systems in the EU database
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your project uses AI and serves the EU market, you need to figure out what risk category it falls into under the EU AI Act and comply accordingly.

requirements.title: Third-Party IP Clearance
requirements.description: Ensure the project does not infringe third-party intellectual property rights
action_steps: Review all third-party components (libraries, APIs, content) for license compliance
Verify trademarks do not conflict with existing marks
If the project name is new, conduct a trademark search before launch
Ensure open-source license obligations are met (attribution, source disclosure if copyleft)
Document all third-party components and their licenses
requirements.plain_language_summary: Check that your project doesn't step on anyone else's intellectual property — especially trademarks, open-source licenses, and third-party content.

requirements.title: Vendor Onboarding Compliance
requirements.description: Complete required due diligence and agreements before engaging a new vendor
action_steps: Complete vendor risk assessment questionnaire
Screen vendor against sanctions lists
Execute appropriate agreements (MSA, DPA, NDA as applicable)
Verify vendor's insurance coverage meets our requirements
Add vendor to the approved vendor list in the procurement system
Set up contract renewal and review reminders
requirements.plain_language_summary: Before working with a new vendor, do your homework: check them out, sign the right agreements, and register them in the system.
